title: Power Pivot: the data model and relationships

videos.script: Lesson 4 answered a question with a lookup. Which origin sold the most? You copied the origin into every sale, one row at a time, with a formula. {{lookup}} That works for one question. Then somebody asks for revenue by customer type. Another lookup column. Then by quarter. Another. The Sales sheet grows sideways, and every new question is a new copy. {{columns}} Power Pivot does it another way. It keeps the tables apart, and you draw a line between them once. Sales in the middle. Products, Customers and a calendar around it. {{star}} Each line joins a code in Sales to the one row that code names. And each line carries a filter. Pick Cerrado in a pivot table, and only the Cerrado sales are added up. {{filter}} This lesson builds that model from your own workbook. You load the three tables. You build a calendar, one row for every day of two years. And you draw three relationships. {{build}} Then you make a pivot table that reads all four tables at once, with no lookup formula anywhere. And you meet the two mistakes that make it show a number that looks fine and is wrong. {{pivot}}
